Use NH3 for complex formation: Cu2+ gives deep blue [Cu(NH3)4]2+. Fe3+ gives brown precipitate with KSCN? Not present. Use H2S acidic to precipitate metal sulfides of heavy metals (Pb2+, Cu2+, Cd2+, Hg2+, etc). Use (NH4)2CO3 for carbonate precipitation of Ca2+, Ba2+, Sr2+ (white precipitate). Use KOH to precipitate Fe(OH)3 (brown), Al(OH)3 (white gelatinous), Zn(OH)2 (white), etc.

We need to identify three cations. Likely common ones: Fe3+, Cu2+, Ni2+, Pb2+, Ca2+, Mg2+, K+, Na+ (but Na not in reagents). Flame test can detect K (violet), Ca (orange-red), Ba (green), Na (yellow). We have K2CrO4 reagent includes K+ but that's fine.
